claim: The organizational integrity of the adaptive immune system is determined by functionally discrete subsets of CD4+ T cells.
source: The organizational integrity of the adaptive immune system is determined by functionally discrete subsets of CD4+ T cells, but it has remained unclear to what extent lineage choice is influenced by clonotypically expressed T-cell receptors (TCRs).
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that frames the study context.

claim: Clonotype fate decisions in CD4+ T cells are linked to the intrinsic properties of somatically rearranged TCRs.

evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the cumulative data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Mycobacterial and viral infections typically elicit T helper 1 (Th1) cells, which produce interferon (IFN)-γ under the control of T-bet.
source: In the classic dichotomy, mycobacterial and viral infections typically elicit T helper 1 (Th1) cells, which produce interferon (IFN)-γ under the control of T-bet, whereas parasitic infections typically elicit Th2 cells, which produce interleukin (IL)-4, IL-5, and IL-13 under the control of GATA3 and STAT6 (Mosmann and Coffman, 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mosmann and Coffman, 1989.

claim: Parasitic infections typically elicit Th2 cells, which produce interleukin (IL)-4, IL-5, and IL-13 under the control of GATA3 and STAT6.
source: In the classic dichotomy, mycobacterial and viral infections typically elicit T helper 1 (Th1) cells, which produce interferon (IFN)-γ under the control of T-bet, whereas parasitic infections typically elicit Th2 cells, which produce interleukin (IL)-4, IL-5, and IL-13 under the control of GATA3 and STAT6 (Mosmann and Coffman, 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mosmann and Coffman, 1989.
